• Terraform creates the store empty and never reads its keys" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="64" width="580" x="100" y="922" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c37" parent="1" style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=11;fontColor=#232F3E;fontStyle=1;" value="Nothing secret in the Terraform state, the Git repository,
the container images or the files the browser receives." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="640" x="40" y="984" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c38" parent="1" style="rounded=0;arcSize=6;html=0;fillColor=#F4F5F7;strokeColor=#232F3E;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=13;fontStyle=1;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=8;spacingTop=4;spacingRight=8;" value="(e) Key decision: no public API" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="220" width="670" x="710" y="810" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c39" parent="1" style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#232F3E;fontStyle=0;" value="The internet only reads pre-built files.

• The browser fetches static files and data/*.json; no endpoint takes input
 or runs code per request.
• No viewer request reaches the lakehouse, Step Functions, Alpaca or
 any other service.
• The publisher runs outside the VPC and accepts no inbound connections:
 only the schedule and the EventBridge rule invoke it.
• Nothing in the VPC accepts inbound connections.
• A leaked password exposes only the study data shown on the site:
 paper-account figures, tickers, model results. It gives no AWS access." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="176" width="640" x="730" y="842" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c40" parent="1" style="rounded=0;arcSize=6;html=0;fillColor=#FFF6EB;strokeColor=#E07000;fontColor=#E07000;fontSize=13;fontStyle=1;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=8;spacingTop=4;spacingRight=8;" value="Known gaps" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="1360" x="20" y="1060" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c41" parent="1" style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#232F3E;fontStyle=0;" value="• One shared password with no lockout or rate limit;
 an AWS WAF rate-based rule is the optional fix.
• HSTS applies only after the first HTTPS response; a new
 browser's very first request can still be plain http (redirected)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="86" width="640" x="40" y="1086" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="c42" parent="1" style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#232F3E;fontStyle=0;" value="• The password hash has no salt; use a long random password.
• The default *.cloudfront.net domain and certificate;
 no custom domain yet." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="86" width="640" x="730" y="1086" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

g.text: Viewer
(untrusted internet)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(247, 243, 255), rgb(28, 25, 35)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(140, 79, 255), rgb(177, 125, 255));

g.text: (a) Edge: CloudFront
CloudFront distribution
• HTTPS only: http gets a 301 redirect to https
• GET and HEAD only: no request writes through it
Function secform4strategy-site-auth (viewer request)
• HTTP Basic auth on every request, before the cache
• fails closed: no header, no stored hash or a wrong
hash returns 401
KeyValueStore secform4strategy-site-auth
• holds only SHA-256 of the authorization header
• the function compares hashes; the password is in
neither the code nor the Terraform state
Response headers policy Managed-SecurityHeadersPolicy
(both cache behaviours)
• HSTS max-age=31536000; X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN
• X-Content-Type-Options nosniff
• Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212));

g.text: HTTPS

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(242, 246, 232), rgb(26, 29, 17)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(122, 161, 22), rgb(97, 130, 11));

g.text: (b) Origin: S3 site bucket
Bucket secform4strategy-site-<account>
• S3 Block Public Access: all four settings on
• SSE-S3 (AES256) encrypts every object at rest
Bucket policy
• s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, only for the
cloudfront.amazonaws.com service principal
• only when AWS:SourceArn is this distribution's ARN;
any other caller gets AccessDenied
Origin Access Control secform4strategy-site
• CloudFront signs every origin request (SigV4, always)

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212));

g.text: SigV4-signed
GetObject

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(253, 241, 242), rgb(36, 26, 27)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(221, 52, 76), rgb(255, 127, 147));

g.text: (c) Identities: each role gets only what its job needs
site-publisher
Lambda

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212));

g.text: assumes
Publisher role secform4strategy-live-site-publisher
• read-only: Step Functions runs, SQS queue attributes,
CloudWatch metrics, schedule state
• reads the lakehouse (Glue, warehouse/) and models/
• read-alpaca-keys: ssm:GetParameters on
/secform4strategy/alpaca-api-key and alpaca-api-secret only
• reads and writes only data/* in the site bucket
• the Alpaca client reads account, positions and orders;
the publisher has no code that places or cancels orders
Cannot: start or stop runs, change queues or schedules,
write the lakehouse or models, write the static files.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(36, 41, 47), rgb(199, 203, 208));

g.text: GitHub Actions
terraform.yml
(master)

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212));

g.text: OIDC
Terraform apply role secform4strategy-github-apply
• the only identity that writes the static site files
• trusts only GitHub OIDC tokens with audience
sts.amazonaws.com and subject
repo:<owner>/SecForm4Strategy:environment:aws
• runs from master, and terraform apply starts only after
a reviewer approves it in the GitHub environment aws
• uploads site/ as aws_s3_object, except data/, fixtures/
and README.md
• one deploy path for infrastructure and site
Cannot: act from a pull request or apply without approval.
No long-lived AWS keys: Lambda and GitHub Actions get temporary credentials from their roles.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(253, 240, 246), rgb(37, 26, 31)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(231, 21, 123), rgb(255, 129, 217));

g.text: (d) Secrets
Alpaca API key and secret: SSM SecureString
/secform4strategy/alpaca-api-key, alpaca-api-secret
• read once at cold start, kept as SecretStr in memory
Site password: only its SHA-256 hash, in the KeyValueStore
• written by scripts/set_site_password.sh from your terminal
• Terraform creates the store empty and never reads its keys
Nothing secret in the Terraform state, the Git repository,
the container images or the files the browser receives.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(244, 245, 247), rgb(25, 26, 27)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(35, 47, 62), rgb(189, 199, 212));

g.text: (e) Key decision: no public API
The internet only reads pre-built files.
• The browser fetches static files and data/*.json; no endpoint takes input
or runs code per request.
• No viewer request reaches the lakehouse, Step Functions, Alpaca or
any other service.
• The publisher runs outside the VPC and accepts no inbound connections:
only the schedule and the EventBridge rule invoke it.
• Nothing in the VPC accepts inbound connections.
• A leaked password exposes only the study data shown on the site:
paper-account figures, tickers, model results. It gives no AWS access.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 246, 235), rgb(32, 24, 15)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(224, 112, 0), rgb(210, 114, 18));

g.text: Known gaps
• One shared password with no lockout or rate limit;
an AWS WAF rate-based rule is the optional fix.
• HSTS applies only after the first HTTPS response; a new
browser's very first request can still be plain http (redirected).
• The password hash has no salt; use a long random password.
• The default *.cloudfront.net domain and certificate;
no custom domain yet.
